subject: Continuity acceptance criteria and cutover constraints
messages:

Cc: Acme Insurance Procurement <procurement@acme-insure.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Initial RFP excerpt — continuity expectations

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our RFP evaluation we're consolidating technical acceptance criteria for continuity and cutover behavior. Two items are especially important to our SRE and procurement teams:

- Target RTO / RPO commitments for your hosted service versus dedicated and private deployments (we need realistic numbers and an explanation of what those guarantees cover).
- Expected failover sequencing for a region-wide outage (time-to-detect, automatic routing, warm-standby activation steps, and manual playbook entry points).

I've attached the RFP excerpt we circulated internally that lists what we need (acme_rfp_excerpt.pdf). Our initial ask is to provide a short (one-page) summary with concrete numbers and an outline of the activation/runbook steps by EOD Friday so we can include it in our vendor comparison.

Also please flag any gaps where you would require a contractual SLA exception or operational runbook addendum.

Best,
Kate Simmons
Director, Infrastructure Risk & Resilience
Acme Insurance

Subject: Re: Initial RFP excerpt — continuity expectations

Hi Kate — thanks for the clear ask and the excerpt. We can put together the one-page summary and an activation matrix; I've attached a working draft (redwood-continuity-summary.pdf) and a short activation matrix CSV for your review (activation-matrix.csv).

High level summary (draft):
- Hosted (Redwood API): Automatic regional routing + global fallback. Typical detection-to-routing time: < 60s. For full service recovery (all backends healthy) we target an RTO of 30 minutes for region failures (automatic fallback may provide continuity faster for many requests). RPO: stateless inference requests — near-zero (requests are handled at call time); for any queued or long-running orchestration the RPO depends on customer-managed state — we'll document expectations.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Cold-replacement RTO for failed pool nodes: 2–6 hours depending on capacity footprint; options for warm standby pools (adds cost) reduce RTO to < 30 minutes. RPO: application-level state replicated per customer policy; Redwood will support cross-region replication for persisted metadata.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): RTO/RPO are deployment-specific; we supply runbooks and orchestration tooling. We recommend a validated warm-standby configuration for customers requiring sub-1-hour RTO.

Key failover sequencing (short):
1) Autonomous detection (monitoring + health checks) -> automatic traffic routing to healthy region/variant.
2) Prefix/KV cache invalidation and rehydration window (best-effort; typically < 2 minutes for cache miss recovery).
3) If automatic fallback insufficient, control-plane-initiated route to Dedicated or Private variant (manual approval required for certain account types).
4) Post-cutover verification and telemetry checks; rollback option if end-to-end validation fails.

Gaps / contractual notes:
- SLA covers regional availability of the Redwood control plane and routing behavior for hosted customers. Customers requiring guaranteed sub-5-minute full-service RTO should evaluate Dedicated with warm-standby or Private deployment and consider an SLA addendum.

I'll schedule a short call to walk through the summary and gather any constraints you want reflected in the final RFP response.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial RFP excerpt — continuity expectations

Jonas / Ben — quick internal note before we finalize the one-pager to Acme:

- We should call out the difference between "service-level continuity" (ability to respond to API calls via routing/fallback) and "operational recovery" (full capacity replacement). Many procurement teams conflate the two.
- Proposed conservative numbers to present: Hosted RTO (service continuity via routing) = 0–30 minutes; Hosted full recovery RTO = 30–90 minutes (depending on failure mode). Dedicated warm standby RTO = <30 minutes; Dedicated cold replacement RTO = 2–6 hours. Private: TBD (explicit in doc).
- Include acceptance test language: we offer a joint dry-run (tabletop + live failover) during the POC window. Acceptance criteria: successful traffic cutover with <5% error amplification and ability to restore original routing within agreed rollback window.

Also add a short paragraph on operational controls: runbook ownership, on-call escalation path, and audit evidence (runbooks, rehearsal logs, telemetry traces).

If that sounds good I can tidy and send.

—Karthik
Head of Platform GTM
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial RFP excerpt — continuity expectations

Kate — following our internal alignment, please find the formalized answers to the two bullets in your excerpt below. I'm pasting the short executive summary here and attaching the finalized one-page document.

Executive summary (final draft):
- Hosted (Redwood API - multi-region, global routing):
  • Detection & automatic routing: automated healthchecks detect degraded region behavior; automated routing cutover typically within 30–90s.
  • Service continuity RTO (automatic routing): typically within 2 minutes for API-level continuity for the majority of traffic.
  • Full functional recovery RTO (control-plane + backend recovery): target 30 minutes (best-effort) with documented escalation if underlying infrastructure requires remediation — contractual SLA for critical accounts available as an addendum.
  • RPO: stateless inference calls are handled at call time (no durable message queueing by default). For customers needing strict RPO guarantees for persisted state (example: batched queued jobs), Redwood supports customer-configured replication for metadata and suggests dedicated deployment patterns.

- Dedicated (Reserved capacity):
  • Warm-standby option: RTO < 30 minutes (additional reserved capacity and cross-region replication enabled).
  • Cold replacement: RTO 2–6 hours depending on the scale of the reserved pool and time to provision replacement instances.
  • RPO: application-level metadata replication (customer-configurable).

- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  • We provide runbooks, orchestration tooling, and can support validated warm-standby configurations; target RTOs are determined during onboarding and captured in the Statement of Work.

Failover sequencing (high-level steps we will provide in the runbook):
1) Detect and classify the event (automated monitoring).
2) Attempt automated traffic routing to healthy region/variant.
3) If traffic routing fails or capacity constraints occur, escalate to control plane to initiate model-variant fallback or dedicated pool promotion.
4) Rehydrate caches and re-run validation checks (end-to-end sampling across common endpoints and token-level latency checks).
5) If cutover validation fails, execute rollback and open a post-incident RCA window.

Acceptance tests and rehearsals:
- Joint tabletop exercise during POC, plus one live rehearsal (non-production) prior to go-live.
- Success criteria: traffic cutover without amplification of errors above 5% vs baseline, and full restoration within agreed rollback window.

Attachments included: redwood-continuity-summary.pdf (one-pager), activation-matrix.csv (cutover sequence), and sample runbook snippets. We can also provide telemetry traces from prior rehearsals on request (redacted).

We are happy to convert these into RFP-friendly RTO/RPO cells for your document and flag the places where contractual exceptions may be required. When would you like to meet to walk the details?

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
